rows.what_the_ink_shows: The sentence clearly has H^{2ν}(X_0) … H^{2ν}(X̄_1), ‘injectif, conoyau engendré par’, followed by a heavily worked cancellation and replacement (crops/56_scan005_L195_cokernel.png). At the far right, a surviving upper loop and a near-vertical descending stem stand alongside a ν-shaped mark above the crossed-out expression (crops/56_scan005_L195_generator.png). The base glyph is partly entangled with the cancellation. This loop-headed form differs visibly from the open, two-legged λ in the local middle-degree table and from λ′_ν at the earlier kernel statement (crops/56_scan005_L195_lambda_comparison.png and crops/56_scan005_L195_lambda_prime_comparison.png). I cannot confidently distinguish a compressed/overwritten λ_ν from a looped ℓ_ν at this locus. In particular, no unambiguous subscript a or explicit ruling-class expression l_a is visible. The original already marks both the cancelled predecessor and λ_ν as doubtful.
rows.note: Retain the existing \deleted{\unsure{\xi}}\unsure{\lambda_\nu} without forcing a certain generator. The main reader also inspected the full scan and all four crops. The looped, overwritten base letter cannot be settled securely; the existing doubt remains adequate, and λ_ν is not asserted to be a certain reading. A looped ℓ-like alternative remains possible, but there is no secure subscript a to support a definite l_a transcription. Classification b describes the conservative textual treatment: L195’s proposed ruling-class generator l_a is a mathematical correction/qualification and is not securely present in the ink. The supplied row says that λ_ν = l_a − l_b represents 2l_a modulo the image and generates the cokernel only when 2 is invertible (for example at an ℓ-adic prime ℓ ≠ 2). This is recorded solely as the supplied mathematical note, not an independently checked proof; it does not resolve the overwritten letter.
